doc.title: Earl Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002

title: Lionel Hampton's money and the three-day drunk
summary: Curtis Lowe's story of Gladys Hampton withholding Hamp's cash.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Yeah I’ve heard Hamp was a little tight fisted.

Yeah, well it was his wife, Gladys, because she wouldn’t let him have any money because he’d go out on a drunk. One time, when Curtis was with the band, one of the times he said that they were always after Gladys. They said, “Gladys, it’s embarrassing. We go out to a nightclub after we finish our dance engagement, and Hamp orders up, and he doesn’t have any money to pay for it. Gee you’ve got to give him an allowance or something.” So one day Hampton got a hold of one of the recording checks. And he disappeared for three days. And when he came back he was wearing the same clothes. He had gone out on a three day drunk. So Gladys said to him, “Now you see why I don’t give him any money.” So that’s the story Curtis told.
